title: Greater Washington Taiwan Culture Center 華府台灣文化中心
content_html:
The Greater Washington Taiwan Culture Center (TCC) is a non-profit 501(c)(3) organization established by Taiwanese Americans in the greater Washington, D.C. area. Located in Rockville, Maryland, near the Shady Grove Metro station, the center serves as a fixed venue for Taiwanese American cultural, civic, and community activities in the mid-Atlantic region.

The idea for the center originated in September 1994, when the Board of Directors of the Washington D.C. Taiwanese Association of America (TAA) appointed former president Dr. Huang Tailang and several community members to form a Taiwan Center Planning Committee. The committee applied for non-profit status in November 1999 under the name “Taiwan Culture Center” and received official recognition in March 2000. In December 2003, the center purchased its current property at 7509 Needwood Road, Derwood, Maryland, a 1.5-acre site, and held its first Open House on January 10, 2004. A public service zoning change was completed in 2008, and in 2016 the center began the design and permitting process for a planned facility expansion.

The center operates a library, office, meeting room, and lounge, and hosts a range of annual programs. Since 2005 it has administered the Taiwanese American Community Scholarship Award (TACSA), open to all graduating high school seniors regardless of ethnicity; as of the most recent reporting, more than 160 graduates have received awards. Since 2009 it has also offered the Janet Chang Memorial Scholarship Award (JCMSA) for first- and second-year Taiwanese American medical school students. The annual Taiwan Night concert, held each May to coincide with Taiwanese American Heritage Week, serves as the setting for the scholarship awards ceremony. Additional programming includes cultural lectures and seminars, a Taiwan Film Appreciation Night, Open Houses in April and September, and free medical consultations organized jointly with the North American Taiwanese Medical Association (NATMA).
